grade.rationale: The implementation is well structured and reasonably testable, but a vulnerability scanner must avoid silent false negatives and uncontrolled traversal. Unsupported JSON is accepted as a clean scan, npm versions can be misattributed, path validation is unsafe on case-sensitive systems, directory links can escape or cycle, and cancellation can leave scanner processes running.

summary: The code is readable and separates command execution from parsing effectively. The principal risks are fail-open parsing, inaccurate npm evidence, unsafe filesystem traversal, incomplete exception handling, abandoned child processes, and all-or-nothing failure behavior that discards useful results. Build analysis reported no findings; test coverage is unknown.

grade.rationale: Unexpected scanner schemas can produce successful empty scans, npm findings can cite an unrelated installed version, and repository containment is incorrect on case-sensitive platforms.
The methods are cohesive and naming is generally clear, but filesystem traversal, schema interpretation, and failure policy embed assumptions that will be difficult to evolve safely.
Control flow and data construction are easy to follow, although the apparent repository-containment guarantee and successful empty parser results conceal important behavior.
Cancellation does not terminate child processes, common filesystem access failures escape the intended unavailable-result path, and one failed target suppresses all previously collected findings.
The injectable command runner and public parsers support focused tests, but direct filesystem access and DateTime.UtcNow remain coupled to global state. No coverage evidence was supplied.

findings.title: Unrecognized scanner JSON is treated as a clean scan
findings.description: ParseDotNet returns no findings whenever the projects property is absent or has the wrong type. ParseNpm similarly returns no findings when neither supported audit structure is present. RunAsync consequently reports the scan as available and clean even if a tool changes its schema or emits an unexpected successful response, creating a silent false negative.
findings.recommendation: Validate a supported schema and required root fields before parsing. Throw a dedicated parse/schema exception for unrecognized output so RunAsync reports the scan as unavailable rather than clean; add fixtures for malformed and future-version payloads.

findings.title: npm findings can report the wrong installed package version
findings.description: ReadNpmVersions records only top-level node_modules entries and stores a single version per package name. npm lockfiles can contain several versions of the same package at different nested paths, so ParseNpm may attach a top-level version to an advisory affecting a nested version, or report no version despite having exact node information. This makes the title, evidence, remediation context, and fingerprint inaccurate.
findings.recommendation: Use the audit entry's affected nodes and resolve each node path against the lockfile packages object. Emit findings for the distinct affected installed versions, or avoid asserting an exact version when it cannot be mapped reliably.

findings.title: Path containment check can accept a sibling directory on case-sensitive systems
findings.description: ResolveTarget always compares paths with OrdinalIgnoreCase. On a case-sensitive platform, a request such as ../Repo can therefore pass validation for a repository rooted at /repo when /Repo is a separate existing sibling directory, allowing the sensor to scan outside the requested repository.
findings.recommendation: Use platform-appropriate path comparison and validate containment by examining a normalized relative path. Reject rooted relative results and any result equal to .. or beginning with a .. directory segment. Address symbolic-link containment separately.

findings.title: Recursive discovery follows directory links without containment or cycle protection
findings.description: FindFiles recursively pushes every non-ignored directory without detecting symbolic links, junctions, previously visited directories, or resolved paths outside the repository. A link can cause external projects to be scanned and commands to run against them; a link to an ancestor can also create unbounded traversal.
findings.recommendation: Define and enforce a link policy. Prefer skipping reparse-point/symbolic-link directories; otherwise resolve link targets, require them to remain under the canonical repository root, and track canonical directory identities to prevent cycles.

findings.title: Cancellation can leave the scanner subprocess running
findings.description: If WaitForExitAsync is cancelled, RunAsync exits and disposes the Process object but does not terminate the underlying child process. A cancelled dotnet or npm audit can therefore continue consuming CPU, holding files, or spawning descendants after the scan has ended.
findings.recommendation: Catch cancellation after a successful start, terminate the process tree when it is still running, wait for termination, and then rethrow the original OperationCanceledException. Ensure output-reading tasks are observed during cleanup.

findings.title: Common filesystem traversal failures bypass the unavailable result
findings.description: Directory enumeration can throw UnauthorizedAccessException and related filesystem exceptions, but RunAsync only converts IOException and a small set of other exceptions into an unavailable result. A repository containing an inaccessible directory can therefore fault the entire sensor call unexpectedly rather than returning structured availability information.
findings.recommendation: Handle expected traversal failures explicitly, either by converting them to an unavailable result with the affected path or by adopting and documenting a safe skip policy. Keep cancellation and programming errors unmasked.

findings.title: One unavailable tool or failed target discards all viable scan results
findings.description: The default configuration requires both tool probes to succeed before any scan runs, and any subsequent project or lockfile failure immediately returns an unavailable result whose findings collection is always empty. Consequently, a missing npm installation can suppress valid .NET analysis, and a late failure discards findings already collected from earlier targets.
findings.recommendation: Represent per-ecosystem and per-target completion explicitly. Preserve findings from successful scans, report diagnostics for failed portions, and mark the result incomplete; alternatively scan only ecosystems detected in the repository unless the configuration explicitly requires others.
